flyfox-exchange.deck: Between the headline promises and the fine print sits FlyFox Exchange. We measured the gap.
flyfox-exchange.depositMethods: Bank cards, bank transfer, PayPal, Skrill
intro: FlyFox Exchange sells a browser-based AI trading desk with a US$250 entry. Before the first deposit, it is worth asking which of the published claims survive contact with the platform own fine print.

The product is browser-based: AI and algorithmic models analyse markets, surface signals and suggest entries, with automatic or manual execution. Registration is free, the demo runs alongside, and the minimum deposit sits at US$250.
The scorecard reflects what the platform publishes, not what its ads promise. We checked the claims against the pages, looked for independent verification, and marked the gaps we found.
whatItClaims: Around-the-clock support through the partner desk.
Signals generated without manual chart reading.
A US$250 minimum deposit to start.
Free registration, with account activation by confirmation link.
Risk settings adjustable before the first live trade.
whatWeChecked: The fee framing: no platform fees, but spreads embedded in every trade.
The support story: around-the-clock coverage claimed, exact figures conflicting.
The geo-restrictions: two lists on the page that do not agree.
The template marks: unfilled placeholders left in the wording.
The performance story: no verified track record behind the return claims.
The number reuse: one score figure doing more than one job.

steps.title: Register
steps.text: Create the account with your contact details, then verify it through the emailed link.

steps.title: Fund
steps.text: Deposit the US$250 minimum by bank card, bank transfer, PayPal or Skrill.

steps.title: Configure
steps.text: Choose your risk level and trading mode, then use the demo to learn the dashboard.

pros: Funding by card, transfer, PayPal and Skrill.
cons: The demo claim buried in the signup flow.
Performance examples without dates or proof.
Asset list that shifts between pages.
The headline fee claim and the real cost disagree.
redFlags: A broker relationship described in one vague sentence.
Ownership details missing from the public pages.
The demo promised in the pitch but buried in the flow.

faqs.a: The platform fee is absent, but every trade carries a broker spread the page itself calls the real cost. The headline says free; the fine print says otherwise. Budget for the fine print.
Yes - signup is free and activates through a confirmation link. The first cost is the US$250 deposit, which stays in your trading balance.

faqs.q: Does it offer a demo account?
faqs.a: Yes - a practice account is part of the package and runs alongside the live balance, which is the sensible first step before risking the US$250 minimum.
The lists conflict - different sections of the site name different countries. Confirm your eligibility with support before depositing.

faqs.q: What happens after I sign up?
faqs.a: You confirm the account by email, fund US$250, set your risk preferences and choose automatic or manual mode. The demo account runs alongside while you learn.

bottomLine: FlyFox Exchange does what it says mechanically - signals, two modes, a broker partner. The open questions are pricing clarity and verification, both solvable by reading before funding.
We scored FlyFox Exchange 4.5 out of 5. The deductions come from the disclosure gaps, not the mechanics. With the US$250 minimum and the demo as guardrails, the risk stays yours to control.
